summary: Harold Scheub studied at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1966–1969). He taught at Valparaiso University (1960–1963), Masindi Senior Secondary School (1963–1965), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2013).
Harold Stewart was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Harold Walter Bailey worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Western Australia and Oxford under Frederick William Thomas, he held posts at SOAS (1929) and Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani was a historian and Indologist. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University, the University of Oxford, and under Ghulam Yazdani. He held posts at Osmania University (~1919–1945), Nizam College (~1945–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).
Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, Hartmut Buescher studied under Chandrabhāl Tripathi. He held positions at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme and served on the faculty at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel worked in Indology. He served at the Prussian State Library's Oriental Department (attested 1992–1994) and directed the Katalogisierung der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (attested 1989).

Haruhiko Masaki specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Gakushuin University and completed master's and doctoral courses at the University of Tokyo, later serving as professor at Nagasaki University from ~1985 to 2004.
Haruka Yanagisawa worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at Chiba University (~1976–1993) and the University of Tokyo (~1993–2007).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her MA (1994) and PhD (2001) at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she was supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Groningen and Leiden under Hans T. Bakker, Tilmann Vetter, and Albrecht Wezler. His posts include Oxford (1995–2000), Pennsylvania (2002–2006), and Hamburg (2000–2002; professor from 2006).

Linguist Harushige Kōzu studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and Musashi University (1968), and led the Classical Society of Japan (1965).

Harvey B. Aronson studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology under Richard Hugh Robinson and others. He was a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988) and served as co-director of the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism (attested 2001).

Haya Akegarasu studied at Otani University, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and under Manshi Kiyozawa and Kyoshi Takahama. He served in Buddhist administrative leadership at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954) and Shinshu Otani-ha (1951–1952).

Heather Stoddard specialized in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1967–1970) with D. C. Lau, as well as under Nicole Vandier-Nicolas and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

Indologist and philosopher Heeraman Tiwari studied at Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1999–), Heidelberg (2011–2012), and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2014–2015).
Hegoda Khemananda worked in Buddhist studies. In 1993, he was attested as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

Heidi Fjeld works in Tibetology. She studied at the University of Oslo, completing her doctoral degree under Signe Howell (~2001–2006), and held a postdoctoral fellowship at the same institution (~2007–2011).
Heidi I. Köppl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer, and also studied under Sherab Zangpo.

Indologist Heidi Pauwels studied at KU Leuven, Vrindaban Research Institute, Cologne, and the University of Washington under Alan W. Entwistle (PhD 1994). She taught at SOAS (1994–1996) and the University of Washington (1996–2009).
